title: Boss: the edge router
summary: Build the brain of an edge router: forwarding, NAT decisions and shortest paths.

steps.title: The edge router
body: Your company's edge router forwards packets, translates addresses and learns paths. Build each part.

steps.title: Forwarding with TTL
prompt: Write a class `Router` with `void Add(string cidr, string via)` and `string Forward(string dst, int ttl)`:
- `ttl <= 1` -> `"drop: ttl exceeded"` (the router would send ICMP time exceeded; that's how traceroute works)
- otherwise the longest prefix match: `"via {via} ttl {ttl - 1}"`
solution: private readonly List<(uint Net, int Prefix, string Via)> routes = new();
static uint ToU(string ip) => ip.Split('.').Aggregate(0u, (acc, o) => (acc << 8) | uint.Parse(o));
static uint Mask(int p) => p == 0 ? 0u : uint.MaxValue << (32 - p);
public void Add(string cidr, string via)
public string Forward(string dst, int ttl)
var best = routes.Where(r => (d & Mask(r.Prefix)) == r.Net).OrderByDescending(r => r.Prefix).ToList();
hints: Store routes as `(uint Net, int Prefix, string Via)`.
Check TTL first, then the longest matching prefix.

steps.title: Port forward or hairpin?
prompt: Write `string Reach(bool fromInside, string dstIp, int dstPort, string publicIp, Dictionary<int, string> forwards, bool hairpinNat)`:
- `dstIp` isn't the router's public IP -> `"routed normally"`
- from inside with hairpin NAT -> `"hairpinned to {target}"`
- from inside without it -> `"fails: no NAT loopback"`
starter: string Reach(bool fromInside, string dstIp, int dstPort, string publicIp, Dictionary<int, string> forwards, bool hairpinNat)
solution: string Reach(bool fromInside, string dstIp, int dstPort, string publicIp, Dictionary<int, string> forwards, bool hairpinNat)
return hairpinNat ? $"hairpinned to {target}" : "fails: no NAT loopback";
template: Dojo.Eq("internet to NAS", "forwarded to 10.0.0.20:443", Reach(false, "203.0.113.1", 443, "203.0.113.1", dojoF, false));
Dojo.Eq("laptop without hairpin", "fails: no NAT loopback", Reach(true, "203.0.113.1", 443, "203.0.113.1", dojoF, false));
Dojo.Eq("laptop with hairpin", "hairpinned to 10.0.0.20:443", Reach(true, "203.0.113.1", 443, "203.0.113.1", dojoF, true));
Dojo.Eq("other destination", "routed normally", Reach(true, "8.8.8.8", 443, "203.0.113.1", dojoF, false));
hints: Check the destination, then the forward, then the direction.
Each rule is one `if` and a `return`.

steps.title: Shortest path
prompt: Write `List<string> ShortestPath(List<(string A, string B, int Cost)> links, string from, string to)` returning the routers on the cheapest path,
`from` first and `to` last, over undirected links, or an empty list if unreachable. Test graphs have no ties.
starter: List<string> ShortestPath(List<(string A, string B, int Cost)> links, string from, string to)
solution: List<string> ShortestPath(List<(string A, string B, int Cost)> links, string from, string to)
string? other = a == next ? b : b == next ? a : null;
if (!dist.TryGetValue(other, out int cur) || d < cur) { dist[other] = d; prev[other] = next; }
template: Dojo.Eq("R1 to R4", new List<string> { "R1", "R2", "R3", "R4" }, ShortestPath(dojoL, "R1", "R4"));
Dojo.Eq("R4 to R1", new List<string> { "R4", "R3", "R2", "R1" }, ShortestPath(dojoL, "R4", "R1"));
hints: Dijkstra again, plus a `prev` dictionary recording where each best cost came from.
Walk `prev` back from `to` to build the path.
